summary: Today’s pulse tracks Europe wildfires: ‘Difficult hours lie ahead’ in battle to contain fires, says Pedro Sánchez as more than 300,000 flee homes in France and Spain, Police hunt for suspect after one killed and 16 injured in attack at Berlin Pride, and What we know so far about the Berlin Pride ramming attack. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are france, people, and hours. In the background, Restricted eating hours may reduce cognitive decline in older age, researchers find and Firefighters in France battle to prevent huge blaze from approaching Bordeaux keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Europe wildfires: ‘Difficult hours lie ahead’ in battle to contain fires, says Pedro Sánchez as more than 300,000 flee homes in France and Spain
headlines.description: Fires displace people on massive scale and trigger one of the largest peacetime civilian evacuation operations ever carried out in France More than 250,000 people flee wildfires in France and Spain As my colleagues note in this story , scientists say climate breakdown is triggering more frequent and more extreme weather events, evaporating soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and leading to thousands of excess deaths . Europe is heating at about twice the global average rate. Spain’s environment ministry has said that 32 major forest fires have been recorded so far this year, compared with seven over the same period in 2025.

headlines.title: Police hunt for suspect after one killed and 16 injured in attack at Berlin Pride
headlines.description: Authorities issue wanted notice for Abdul Ballout, 21, after deadly van ramming described as Islamist terrorism German authorities have issued a wanted notice for a suspect in a deadly van ramming near Berlin’s Pride festival that has been described as an Islamist attack. The interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, named the chief suspect as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout. German media reported he was a supporter of Islamic State with a criminal conviction in May.

headlines.title: What we know so far about the Berlin Pride ramming attack
headlines.description: A police manhunt is under way after a suspect rammed a car into a crowd at a Pride event in the German capital on Saturday night.

headlines.title: Restricted eating hours may reduce cognitive decline in older age, researchers find
headlines.description: Preliminary study shows older people who avoided food four hours before bed did better in problem solving tests Confining mealtimes and snacks to a nine-hour window and avoiding food for four hours before bed may help stave off cognitive decline in older age, researchers say. A pilot study of older women living with overweight or obesity found hints of improvement in mental skills among those who ate within the restricted period compared with those who spread their meals over a longer time.

headlines.title: Firefighters in France battle to prevent huge blaze from approaching Bordeaux
headlines.description: Efforts to contain wildfire that has consumed an area of four times the size of Paris impeded by windy conditions Europe wildfires live – latest updates Authorities are battling to contain a huge wildfire near Bordeaux in south-west France that has consumed an area of land four times the size of Paris. Efforts to extinguish the blaze in the Gironde region, where nearly 220,000 people have been evacuated, were hampered by windy conditions on Saturday night.

headlines.title: Loyal to the look: why Zohran Mamdani wears a suit in all seasons
headlines.description: Around town, on the pitch and even in the pool, the New York mayor keeps his suit on – what do his sartorial choices Playing football. Playing in the sand . Dancing on a stage with Alicia Keys and the entire New York Knicks roster. Swimming in a swimming pool. Swimming in the ocean. Traditionally, a suit and tie would be considered inappropriate attire for each of these activities. Yet over the past year Zohran Mamdani has seemingly been on a one-man crusade to prove otherwise: to convince people that a formal suit is, actually, suitable for all activities.

headlinePool.title: Is Burnham’s Oxbridge-heavy cabinet a sign of social mobility or lack of progress on class?
headlinePool.description: PM’s team can be seen as backward step even though in some ways it is more diverse. Yet its makeup points to wider access to power Race, school, gender: the makeup of Andy Burnham’s cabinet – in charts Like 20 British prime ministers before him, Andy Burnham’s new cabinet minister for AI, Kanishka Narayan, went to Eton. After graduating from the country’s most elite private school, Narayan attended Balliol College, Oxford, where he studied – what else? – PPE (politics, philosophy and economics), like David Cameron, Rishi Sunak, Ed Miliband and a host of other senior politicians . An MBA at Stanford and a career in the City followed. But Narayan’s background is hardly typical of the British ruling class . Born in Bihar in eastern India, he moved with his family to Cardiff when he was 12. He and his younger brother were sleeping on the floor of their one-bedroom home when a teacher at his local high school suggested the bright young boy apply for some private schools. His parents, who had joined the Labour party almost as soon as they arrived in Wales, ran a petrol station. Eton was possible only thanks to a full scholarship.

headlinePool.title: RFK Jr urges Alzheimer’s screening but blunts key panel that could drive research
headlinePool.description: Experts say evidence for cognitive screening desired by health secretary ‘not great’ as taskforce idle since last year The US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, has called for better Alzheimer’s screening – but a critical federal panel that might have helped researchers find practical ways to do that has been prevented from meeting for more than a year. The panel, formally called the US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF), had planned to issue a recommendation on screening for cognitive decline this year, alongside 13 other topics as varied as autism screening and food allergy prevention.

headlinePool.title: Israeli settlers set fire to mosques, cars and farm land in West Bank, Palestinians say
headlinePool.description: The latest attacks come two days after a clash between settlers and Palestinians near the village of Tell, which left four Palestinians and two Israelis dead.

headlinePool.title: Trump revives old tropes as he pushes warnings of ‘communist menace’
headlinePool.description: President harks back to red scare of his childhood to attack US left – but will such language resonate beyond Maga base? Perhaps above all else, Donald Trump is a child of the cold war. Three months before the US president was born, Winston Churchill delivered a historic speech in Fulton, Missouri, that ushered in a generations-long existential struggle between western capitalism and Soviet communism.

headlinePool.title: Rage-giving, innovation and cuts: How public media has survived without federal funds
headlinePool.description: A year after President Trump signed a law ending six decades of federal funding of public media, it's a time of reinvention, innovation and clear anxiety at public tv and radio stations nationwide.

headlinePool.title: Lebanese displaced by war turn to satellites to check their homes
headlinePool.description: Unable to return home, some Lebanese displaced by Israel's invasion of southern Lebanon are buying satellite images to see whether their houses survived.

headlinePool.title: Andy Burnham says he will disagree with Trump in public if necessary
headlinePool.description: PM promises to ‘defend national interest before anything else’ in first big broadcast interview since entering No 10 Andy Burnham has promised to disagree with Donald Trump if necessary, including in public, in his first big broadcast interview since becoming prime minister. Burnham’s comments came as Wes Streeting, the new defence secretary, said he did not believe the Trump administration was looking for allies who “suck up”, but rather those with the confidence to set out disagreements when needed.

headlinePool.title: Climate change is now threatening a pillar of childhood: summer break
headlinePool.description: When summer rolls around, many parents scramble to sign up their young kids for outdoor activities. But what do you do when extreme heat and wildfire smoke increasingly make the outdoors dangerous?
